newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Ousted Afghan forces attack strategic pass to Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Afghan forces attack strategic pass to Kabul.

text.p: Forces belonging to the ousted Afghan government launched an attack on a strategic pass leading to Kabul on Sunday using rockets, artillery and planes in a bid to take it from the Taleban.

"We are very busy now," said General Abdul Rauf Begi, commander of forces on the front line belonging to northern Uzbek leader Abdul Rashid Dostum, now allied to ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood.
Begi, a Russian map spread out before him, directed shells and rockets onto Taleban positions in the barren hills below the De Sabz pass, 30 km (19 miles) north of Kabul.
One of Masood's commanders, Sayid Akbar, said two planes belonging to Dostum bombed Taleban positions on the hill early on Sunday morning.
He said the attack began at 6.00 a.m (0130 GMT) and there appeared to be little or no return fire from the Taleban.
Positions around a second pass leading to Kabul, Khair Khana, which lies 15 km (nine miles) north of the capital, were said by commanders to be quiet.
Masood and Dostum formally joined forces two weeks ago to fight the Islamic Taleban movement, which swept into Kabul last month forcing Masood to retreat northward to these hills.
The front lines north of the capital have been static for a week.

In Kabul witnesses said warplanes, apparently belonging to the Masood-Dostum alliance, screamed overhead at night and on Sunday morning, dropping bombs on the airport and setting off furious barrages of anti-aircraft fire.
The raids, the first on Kabul since the Taleban took over, were the latest sign that hopes for an early ceasefire are dead.
